title: Phase 4: Signature anchoring + triggers — sig-winid capture, lifecycle, CursorHold opt-in, activeParameter sync, hint extmark
notes:
- Anchor float built from RAW results via stable utils (convert_*_to_markdown_lines + open_floating_preview, close_events={}) — NOT the deprecated builtin handler capture from the original plan
- Fallback chain: signatureHelp (only answers inside call parens) → hover (answers anywhere on symbol) → cursor anchor
- float.below() computes editor-grid anchor: win_get_position + height + 2 border rows; ts width >= sig width for connected look
- activeParameter → roots[idx+1].active when kind=param, rendered TypeScopeActive
- CursorHold trigger (trigger='hover' via setup): suppression key = buf:line:cword, silent mode (no notify spam)
- hint.lua: eol virt_text '▸ typescope' per resolved call line, ui.hint config gate
- M.hover(): K-takeover — typescope for functions, vim.lsp.buf.hover() fallback via on_unresolved; double-K focuses

close_reason: Root cause: vim.lsp.util.open_floating_preview hardcodes a BufLeave autocmd (ignores close_events={}) closing the preview when ANY third buffer is entered — focusing the TypeScope float qualified, and our either-float-dies-both-die cascade closed the rest. No borrowed machinery left in the float path; K takeover remains scoped to Tony's python mapping.

title: Phase 5: Heuristic examples — pattern table, cache, e toggle
notes:

title: Alias expansion: chase type aliases (X = Literal[...], type X = ...) into expandable nodes
description: Definition on an alias lands on an assignment, not class_definition — type_at returns nil and we leaf out at the name. Parse the RHS as an annotation instead (pure TS, no extra LSP). Covers TypeAlias annotations and 3.12 type statements. From Tony's declared-vs-evaluated discussion 2026-07-26.
close_reason: alias_at in extract/python.lua recognizes X = Class / X = A | B / X = Optional[T] / X: TypeAlias = ... / 3.12 type X = ... (field 'right'); rejects calls, value literals, non-TypeAlias annotated assignments, positions not on the LHS name. attach_type's failed-class path tries the alias hop (typeshed-guarded, ancestry includes the alias loc so X=Y,Y=X chains terminate): RHS parsed via annotation(), refs chased at SAME depth with force_single when the alias has one ref — fields attach directly under the aliased node, alias name stays as displayed vocabulary. Pure-Literal aliases unchanged (0 refs → wuf's ≈ decoration still handles display). Badges/inheritance/examples survive the hop (e2e: Payload = UserRecord shows email/age + NotRequired). uvicorn regression: no dupes, ~810ms open (within noise of the 770ms wuf baseline).

description: From Tony (2026-07-29) while confirming word-based CursorHold re-fire. Candidates: (1) session cache of resolved class structures keyed on loc/model.hash — repeated opens of the same function or type currently re-chase everything; (2) parallelize the per-leaf hover fan-out (wuf) — ~8 sequential hovers contribute to the ~800ms uvicorn.run open, and coroutine-parallel requests are the obvious lever; (3) parsed-buffer reuse for typeshed-adjacent .py files; (4) measure CursorHold-mode request volume in real editing before optimizing it. title: Phase 6: LLM examples — Ollama, spinner, fallback
notes: TIMEOUT ROOT CAUSE (Tony live repro #2, 2026-07-30): NOT cold model (api/ps showed resident, 0.5s/request) — GENERATION LENGTH. A 48-leaf uvicorn.run float = 600-800 output tokens = 30s+ at 22tok/s; no per-request timeout survives, and ollama cancels generation on curl disconnect so nothing caches and the retry restarts from zero = permanent failure loop on big floats. Fix: LLM_BATCH=8 leaves per request, sequential chain, PROGRESSIVE fill — on_progress fires per landed batch (callers re-render), example_kind flipped upfront (render falls back to heuristics until values arrive), partial success reported honestly if a later batch dies, completed batches always cache. keep_alive=30m on generate+warmup keeps the model resident through a session. Measured: uvicorn.run auto-mode opens 0.9s, fully filled ~20s in visible waves.

title: Declaration fallback: retry textDocument/declaration when definition doesn't land on a def (getpass case)
description: basedpyright resolves stdlib names to runtime impl where the name may be a conditional assignment (getpass = unix_getpass). Retry with declaration → typeshed stub → annotated signature parses fine. Discovered by Tony testing shot_crud.py:137.
notes:
- Root cause: textDocument/definition is a RUNTIME question; basedpyright sends stdlib getpass to getpass.py where the name is a conditional assignment (getpass = unix_getpass), not a def
- Fix: when function_info finds no function_definition, retry once with textDocument/declaration (static universe → typeshed stub → annotated def, same parse path)
- Second fix from same session: typeshed guard extended to runtime stdlib (/lib/pythonX.Y/ minus site-packages) — TextIO's definition lands in runtime typing.py which contains no 'typeshed' in path
- Empty variant children (resolved class, zero fields+methods) no longer added
- Hygiene: extractor looked up by filetype not hardcoded 'python'; lazy hooks carry their impl ref
- Mock server now serves declaration (defs only) vs definition (alias assignments win) to mimic basedpyright; fixtures prompting.py/prompting_stub.py reproduce the getpass shape
- Verified against real basedpyright on shot_crud.py:137: renders prompt/stream/returns from stub
